_meta.purpose: Page grammar for ONE step of a multi-step flow: progress indicator, the step itself, the Back/Next row.

progress.note: Exactly one progress indicator, directly after the Header. Stepper when the steps have meaningful names, progress bar otherwise.

step.note: The current step. On the last frame use the confirmation instead.

nav.note: Back/Next for every step frame. The FIRST step has nothing to go back to, so it uses process.navigation-first-section: a SINGLE right-aligned action, not a spread row. Omit the slot entirely on the confirmation frame — it carries its own single action.

rules: ONE rendered frame per step. A flow of four steps is four separate frames, each a complete screen with progress, step and nav.
Prototyping is out of scope: deliver static frames and say so. Never wire reactions or flow starting points between them.
Exactly one Brand action per frame — Next on a step, the follow-up action on the confirmation. Back is ghost.
The confirmation frame replaces the step and drops the Back/Next row.
The progress indicator is identical on every frame of the flow except for its state; do not switch between stepper and progress bar mid-flow.

A row with a SINGLE action is right-aligned (align: "right"), never `spread: true` — spread distributes two ends, and with one child it renders flush left. This is the first step, whose `Zurück` is dropped.
Determinate progress uses the real DB progress component, which offers only 25, 50 and 75 percent. Any other value is a hard stop.
Input controls inside a step reuse the form page-type blocks; do not invent new field fragments here.
